label: prf:frobenius-relation
title: Proof of Frobenius relation
html:
The Frobenius form \int_A and the multiplication \mu together define a non-degenerate pairing \langle a, b \rangle = \int_A(\mu(a \otimes b)) (Frobenius pairing). Non-degeneracy gives a copairing \gamma = \sum_i \gamma_i' \otimes \gamma_i'' \in A \otimes A, the unique element satisfying the snake identity \sum_i \langle a, \gamma_i' \rangle\, \gamma_i'' = a for all a \in A. The comultiplication dual to \mu under the pairing is

  \Delta_\mu = (\mu \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes \gamma),
  \qquad
  \Delta_\mu(b) = \sum_i \mu(b \otimes \gamma_i') \otimes \gamma_i'' .

That this map is the transpose of \mu under the pairing is the standard equivalence of the two descriptions of the comultiplication of a Frobenius algebra ([kock2004], §2.3); it uses only the snake identity.

With this form the relation is associativity. For a, b \in A,

  (\mu \otimes \mathrm{id})\bigl(a \otimes \Delta_\mu(b)\bigr)
  = \sum_i \mu\bigl(a \otimes \mu(b \otimes \gamma_i')\bigr) \otimes \gamma_i''
  = \sum_i \mu\bigl(\mu(a \otimes b) \otimes \gamma_i'\bigr) \otimes \gamma_i''
  = \Delta_\mu\bigl(\mu(a \otimes b)\bigr).

Hence (\mu \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes \Delta_\mu) = \Delta_\mu \circ \mu. \square
